rationale:
The phone field is split into three separate s and #phone-area carries no label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title; the visible 'Phone' text is a plain

with no programmatic association. The area-code control therefore has no programmatically determinable accessible name, so a screen reader announces only 'edit, blank'. This is the per-control NAME failure of F68, not a group-instruction issue.
citation: Failure F68: 'Failure of Success Criterion 4.1.2 due to a user interface control not having a programmatically determined name.' Each split sub-input is a user interface control needing its own name.

rationale: The date is three bare inputs whose only textual hint is a placeholder ('MM'). A placeholder is not an accessible name: it is not exposed as the control's name and disappears on input, so #dob-month has no programmatically determined name. Each of Month/Day/Year is a distinct control that 4.1.2 requires to be individually named.
citation: SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A): 'For all user interface components ... the name and role can be programmatically determined ...'. A placeholder does not provide that name.

rationale: The SSN is three inputs with no label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title, and the 'Social Security Number' text is an unassociated <div>. #ssn1 has no programmatically determinable name, so an assistive technology cannot tell the user which segment it is. Every form input needs a determinable name under the Trusted Tester 4.1.2 condition.
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 condition for 4.1.2: every form input has a programmatically determinable accessible name; a split field's parts each need a name or an unambiguous group name.

rationale: Six single-character OTP boxes carry no label, aria-label, or title, and there is no role=group with a name. input[name='otp1'] is a control with no programmatically determined name, announced as 'edit, blank'. Each digit box is an individual user interface component that must be named under 4.1.2.
citation: Failure F68: 'Failure of Success Criterion 4.1.2 due to a user interface control not having a programmatically determined name.'

rationale:
The card number is split into four 4-digit inputs with no per-input name and no group name; the 'Card number' text is a loose

. #cc1 has no programmatically determinable accessible name, so its role as 'first group of the card number' is not conveyed. Technique H44 (label for) or ARIA16 (aria-labelledby) would be required to name each control.
citation: Technique H44: 'Using label elements to associate text labels with form controls.' Absent any such association, the control lacks the name 4.1.2 requires.

rationale: The time field is an hour input and a minute input with no name on either; the ':' separator is aria-hidden. #time-hh exposes no accessible name, so assistive technology cannot distinguish the hour control from the minute control. Each is a separate control that 4.1.2 requires to be named.
citation: SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A): '... the name and role can be programmatically determined ...'. Neither split time control has a determinable name.

rationale: Only the first sub-input (#exp-month) is labelled 'Card expiry'; #exp-day and #exp-year have only placeholders and no label/aria-label/title. #exp-day therefore has no programmatically determined name, so 4.1.2 fails for that control even though a sibling control is named. The first control being named does not name the others.
citation: Failure F68: 'Failure of Success Criterion 4.1.2 due to a user interface control not having a programmatically determined name.' Applies independently to each of the split inputs.

rationale: The 'ZIP' and '+4' captions are loose <span>s with no for/id or aria-labelledby tying them to the inputs, so they convey nothing programmatically. #zip-main has no accessible name; sighted proximity does not make a programmatic name. 4.1.2 requires the name to be programmatically determinable, which adjacent untied text is not.
citation: SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A): '... the name and role can be programmatically determined ...'. Visually adjacent text that is not programmatically associated does not provide that name.

rationale: A role=group wraps the two phone inputs but the group has no aria-label or aria-labelledby, and the inputs themselves carry no name. #mob-area has no programmatically determined name and there is not even a group name to fall back on, so 4.1.2 fails at the control level. role=group without a name adds no naming information.
citation: Failure F68: 'Failure of Success Criterion 4.1.2 due to a user interface control not having a programmatically determined name.'

rationale: Each routing-number input has a <label for> correctly wired, but every label is empty, so it contributes no text to the accessible name. #rt1 ends up with an empty name, which fails 4.1.2 the same as having no label at all. The presence of a label element is not sufficient; it must contain a text label per H44.
citation: Technique H44: 'Using label elements to associate text labels with form controls.' An empty label element associates no text, so the control has no name.

rationale: Each account-number input uses aria-labelledby but the referenced ids (e.g. 'lbl-acct1') do not exist in the DOM, so the reference resolves to nothing and no name is computed. #acct1 therefore has no programmatically determined name. A dangling aria-labelledby does not satisfy ARIA16.
citation: Technique ARIA16: 'Using aria-labelledby to provide a name for user interface controls.' The technique requires the referenced id to exist and contain text; a broken reference provides no name.

rationale: A single 'Sort code' <label for='sc1'> names only the first input; #sc2 and #sc3 have no label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title. #sc2 has no programmatically determined name, so 4.1.2 fails for it. One label cannot name three distinct controls; each split input needs its own name.
citation: Trusted Tester 5.1 condition for 4.1.2: every form input has a programmatically determinable accessible name; a single label for one part leaves the other parts unnamed.

rationale: Each phone part has its own <label for> ('Area code', 'Prefix', 'Line number'), so #ph-area has a clear, unique, programmatically determined accessible name. Every split control is individually named, satisfying 4.1.2 at the control level via H44.
citation: Technique H44: 'Using label elements to associate text labels with form controls.' Each sub-input is associated with a distinct visible label.

rationale: Each date input has its own aria-label ('Month'/'Day'/'Year') and the whole field is wrapped in a fieldset with legend 'Date of birth'. #dob-month has a programmatically determined name ('Month'), and the group name supplies additional context. The per-control name requirement of 4.1.2 is met.
citation: SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A): '... the name and role can be programmatically determined ...'. aria-label supplies each control's name; the legend supplies the group name.

rationale: Each OTP box has an aria-label ('Digit 1'..'Digit 6') and they sit inside a role=group named 'Verification code'. input[name='otp3'] has the programmatically determined name 'Digit 3', so each control is uniquely named and 4.1.2 passes for every box.
citation: Technique ARIA16 / SC 4.1.2: each control's name is programmatically determined via aria-label, and the named group provides surrounding context.

rationale: Each SSN part has a <label for> ('First three digits'/'Middle two digits'/'Last four digits'). #ssn3 has the programmatically determined name 'Last four digits', distinguishing it from the other segments. All split controls are named, so 4.1.2 passes.
citation: Technique H44: 'Using label elements to associate text labels with form controls.'

rationale: The phone field is inside a fieldset with legend 'Phone number' and each input carries a title ('Area code'/'Prefix'/'Line number'). #ph-prefix has the programmatically determined name 'Prefix' via its title (H65), and the legend names the group. Each control is named, so 4.1.2 passes.
citation: Technique H65: 'Using the title attribute to identify form controls when the label element cannot be used.' The title supplies each control's accessible name.

rationale: Each card-number input uses aria-labelledby referencing the group heading id ('Card number') plus a per-part id ('group 2'), which concatenate into a unique name. #cc2 has the programmatically determined name 'Card number group 2', so each split control is named. 4.1.2 passes via ARIA16.
citation: Technique ARIA16: 'Using aria-labelledby to provide a name for user interface controls.' Multiple referenced ids concatenate into the control's name.

rationale: The hour and minute inputs each have their own <label for> ('Hour'/'Minute'). #time-mm has the programmatically determined name 'Minute', distinguishing it from the hour control. Both split controls are named, satisfying 4.1.2.
citation: Technique H44: 'Using label elements to associate text labels with form controls.'

rationale: The phone number is a single combined control, not split into parts, and it has a <label for> 'Phone number (including area code)'. #phone-full has a clear programmatically determined name; there are no separate unnamed sub-inputs to fail 4.1.2. A non-split named control trivially passes.
citation: Technique H44 / SC 4.1.2: the one control has a programmatically determined name via its associated label.

rationale: The postcode is segmented into outward and inward inputs, each with a real visible <label for> ('Outward code'/'Inward code'). #pc-in has the programmatically determined name 'Inward code', so each segment is individually named and 4.1.2 passes.
citation: Technique H44: 'Using label elements to associate text labels with form controls.'

rationale: Each OTP box uses aria-labelledby pointing at its own visible caption ('1st digit'..'4th digit') inside a role=group named 'One-time passcode'. input[name='d3'] has the programmatically determined name '3rd digit', so each control is uniquely named. 4.1.2 passes via ARIA16.
citation: Technique ARIA16: 'Using aria-labelledby to provide a name for user interface controls.'

rationale: Each card-expiry input is wrapped inside a <label> whose text ('Expiry month'/'Expiry year') implicitly associates with the nested control. #exp-mm has the programmatically determined name 'Expiry month', so each split control is named without needing a for/id. 4.1.2 passes.
citation: Technique H44: 'Using label elements to associate text labels with form controls.' Implicit (wrapping) association names the nested input.

rationale: Although the browser renders a native date control as M/D/Y spinners, the DOM exposes a single <input type='date'> with a <label for> 'Date of birth'. #dob has a programmatically determined name and the user agent manages the segment semantics internally, so there are no separate unnamed author-provided inputs. 4.1.2 passes.
citation: EN 301 549 clause 9.4.1.2 (maps to WCAG 4.1.2): the single native control has a programmatically determined name via its label.

rationale: A fieldset/legend names the GROUP ('Phone number') but #ph-prefix has no individual label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title. Whether the group name alone satisfies 4.1.2 for each control is a genuine grey area: F68 reads name at the per-control level (the control's own name is empty), yet some interpret the legend as naming each part via grouping context. The runner should abstain rather than force a verdict.
citation: Technique H71 / G131: a descriptive group label (fieldset/legend) for related controls; whether that group label substitutes for each control's own programmatic name under F68 is the disputed point.

rationale: A role=group with aria-label 'Date of birth' names the group, but #dob-day has no per-control name (placeholder only). It is arguable whether the group name discharges 4.1.2 for each split input or whether F68 still applies because the control's own accessible name is empty. This sits between 'named via context' and a per-control name failure, so abstain is the honest disposition.
citation: SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A): '... the name and role can be programmatically determined ...'. Whether a group name programmatically determines each member control's name is the genuinely disputed question.

rationale: The OTP group is named 'Verification code' via role=group + aria-label, but input[name='otp4'] has no per-box name. A screen reader announces the group name on entry, yet each box's own accessible name is empty. Whether group-name-only meets 4.1.2 for each of the six controls (or fails per F68) is a real grey area, so the runner should abstain.
citation: Failure F68 vs Technique H71/G131: F68 reads the name at the individual control; H71/G131 names the group. The tension between them is precisely why this case is ambiguous.
